name: Kangla
summary: Historic seat of Manipur governance and the defining heritage site of the state, in the centre of Imphal.
overview: Kangla sits on the bank of the Imphal river and was the traditional seat of Manipuri rulers. Its ceremonial gateways, temples, moats and open lawns make it the single best starting point for understanding how the Manipur valley organised itself politically and ritually. It rewards a slow, guided visit rather than a quick photograph stop.
accessibilityNotes: Largely level ground with wide paths. Some structures have steps without ramps.

name: Ima Keithel
summary: Historic all-women market in central Imphal and one of the most distinctive cultural experiences in the region.
overview: Ima Keithel, the mothers market, is run entirely by women traders across handloom, produce, fish, household goods and prepared food. It is a living institution rather than a monument, and it is the most direct way for a visitor to meet Manipuri commerce, textiles and food in one place.
accessibilityNotes: Ground floor aisles are navigable. Upper levels are reached by stairs and are narrow when busy.

name: Loktak Lake
summary: The largest freshwater lake in the region and the signature landscape of Manipur, known for its floating phumdi islands.
overview: Loktak is a working landscape as much as a view. Circular phumdi, floating mats of vegetation and soil, support fishing households whose livelihoods depend on the health of the lake. Sunrise from the Sendra side is the classic photograph, but the more interesting visit is the one that explains what phumdi are and why the lake needs careful use.
accessibilityNotes: Viewpoints are reachable by road. Boat transfers require stepping down into small craft.

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
summary: Floating national park on the southern reach of Loktak, associated with the Sangai deer and its wetland habitat.
overview: Keibul Lamjao is described as the only floating national park of its kind: the habitat itself is a mass of phumdi. It is the natural companion visit to Loktak and turns a scenic trip into an ecology lesson about a habitat that depends on water level management.
accessibilityNotes: Watchtower access involves stairs. Trails are uneven and can be wet.

name: Moirang
summary: Historic town on the Loktak side, associated with both the Khamba-Thoibi tradition and Second World War history.
overview: Moirang carries two distinct layers of meaning: the Khamba-Thoibi cultural tradition centred on the Thangjing shrine, and the Second World War history associated with the Indian National Army. Visited together with Loktak, it turns a lake trip into a half-day narrative.
accessibilityNotes: Museum and memorial areas are mostly level with some steps.

name: Ukhrul
summary: Hill district headquarters with strong nature, Tangkhul cultural and community tourism potential.
overview: Ukhrul is the base for the eastern hills: cool weather, terraced slopes, village homestays and a distinct Tangkhul cultural life. It has the room and the community interest to take more visitors than it currently receives, which makes it the clearest candidate for demand diversification away from the valley.
bestSeason: March to May and September to November
accessibilityNotes: Hill roads with gradients. Village walks involve slopes and uneven paths.

name: Shirui
summary: Mountain and biodiversity destination associated with the Shirui lily and its restricted habitat.
overview: The Shirui hill range is known for a lily that grows in a very limited habitat. Its fame is also its risk: visitor pressure in the flowering window has to be managed carefully, which makes Shirui a good place to demonstrate responsible, capacity aware promotion.
bestSeason: May to June for the flowering window
accessibilityNotes: Requires a sustained uphill trek. Not suitable for low mobility visitors.

name: Andro
summary: Cultural village east of Imphal known for pottery, traditional practice and a living craft heritage.
overview: Andro is a scholar village for anyone interested in craft: pottery made without a wheel, a preserved cultural complex and household level practice that visitors can watch and try. It is a strong half-day pairing with Imphal and routes tourist spending directly to artisan households.
accessibilityNotes: Village paths are mostly level but unpaved in places.

name: Khongjom
summary: Memorial site of the 1891 Anglo-Manipuri conflict and the anchor of a state history trail.
overview: Khongjom is where the Anglo-Manipuri War of 1891 reached its final stand. The hillside memorial is central to how Manipur remembers that period, and Khongjom Day remains an important commemoration. It works best as part of a history route rather than a standalone stop.
accessibilityNotes: The memorial is approached by a flight of steps up the hillside.

name: Moreh
summary: Border town with a multicultural trading character and cross-border commerce history.
overview: Moreh sits on the India-Myanmar border and has a mixed population and market culture shaped by trade. Visitor access and permitted activity depend on prevailing border and security regulations, so any promotion of Moreh has to be checked against current advisories.
accessibilityNotes: Long road journey from Imphal. Market areas are congested.

name: Imphal War Cemetery
summary: Commonwealth war cemetery in Imphal and the anchor point of the Second World War heritage route.
overview: The Imphal War Cemetery commemorates Commonwealth personnel who died in the 1944 campaign around Imphal. It is quiet, carefully maintained and pairs naturally with Moirang and the wider Second World War circuit that draws specialist visitors from outside the region.
accessibilityNotes: Level lawns and paved paths throughout.

name: Dzukou Valley
summary: High valley on the Manipur-Nagaland boundary, reached on foot and known for seasonal flowering meadows.
overview: Dzukou is a trekking destination, not a drive-up viewpoint. The valley floor is a rolling meadow cut by a stream, and the walk in is the experience. Because it straddles a state boundary and has fragile ground cover, visitor numbers and fire risk both need active management.
bestSeason: June to September for flowering, October to December for clear weather
accessibilityNotes: Full day trek with steep sections. Not suitable for low mobility or senior visitors.

name: Tamenglong
summary: Western hill district with waterfalls, caves, orange country and strong community eco-tourism potential.
overview: Tamenglong is the least developed of the nature destinations of the state in tourism terms, with waterfalls, cave systems and an annual orange harvest tradition. Low current demand and untested visitor infrastructure make it a long horizon development candidate rather than a next month campaign target.
accessibilityNotes: Long hill drives and unpaved approaches to most natural sites.

name: Bishnupur Temple
summary: Historic brick temple that gives Bishnupur district its name, on the road between Imphal and Loktak.
overview: The Vishnu temple at Bishnupur is an early brick structure whose form reflects influences from beyond the valley. It sits directly on the route most visitors already take to Loktak, which makes it an easy addition that spreads visitor time across more of the district.
accessibilityNotes: Short walk from the road with a raised temple platform reached by steps.
